why: A check failed: PostgreSQL 10 renamed the functions with xlog in their names to wal (and location to lsn), so on every Aurora PostgreSQL line the call fails with an unknown function when the routine runs. Fix: Call the new name: pg_current_wal_lsn() for pg_current_xlog_location(), pg_walfile_name() for pg_xlogfile_name(), pg_wal_lsn_diff() for pg_xlog_location_diff(), pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() for pg_last_xlog_replay_location(), and so on.

rules.reason: A function's CREATE statement names no owner, so on Aurora PostgreSQL the routine is owned by the user that creates it; the record names that user in place of the source owner, and the statement does not change; a SECURITY DEFINER routine then runs with the target user's privileges, and its record says so.
